t.en: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards, like ABA or RACECAR. If you delete some letters from a word (the rest keep their order), what is the longest palindrome you can leave? From CHARACTER, for example, you can leave CARAC.

A new table: the interval table. Cell (i, j) holds the answer for “the stretch from letter i to letter j”. Only the upper-right half is used, because a stretch always starts to the left of where it ends. The top-right corner is the answer for the whole word.
The diagonal holds single letters, each a palindrome of length 1 on its own, already filled in. The line just under the diagonal is “empty runs” with no letters at all, filled with 0.

The robot stands on (i, j): the cell to the left is the stretch without its right end, the cell below is the stretch without its left end, and down-left is the stretch without both ends. The This cell panel has “ends match”. Look only at the two letters at the ends, and think what to do when they match and when they don’t.
This robot scans by length: first every shortest stretch, then the longer ones, one diagonal at a time towards the top-right corner.

goal.en: Find the longest palindromic subsequence in each word: the longest string, left after deleting some letters, that reads the same forwards and backwards.

how.en: Build the circuit and click “Run tests”. The robot scans by length, so a long stretch only ever reads shorter stretches that are already computed.

body.en: Every cell of an interval table is computed from shorter stretches: with one end dropped, or both. So the short stretches have to come first: this machine goes by length from shortest to longest.
CHARACTER hides CARAC, and BBABCBCAB hides BABCBAB. Finding palindromic structures in DNA uses exactly this table.

note.en: Interval table: (i, j) holds the answer for a stretch, computed from shorter stretches.

hints.en: When the ends match, both can stay. Which stretch is left, and how much do you add? Use a Pass gate with “ends match” as its condition.
When the ends differ, at least one has to go: drop the right end (left) or the left end (down), and take the larger. Wire all three into “max”.
No need to worry about the order: left, down and down-left are all shorter stretches, and since the robot scans by length they are always computed first.
